newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. officials in Shanghai visit jailed businessman.
newsitem.headline: U.S. officials in Shanghai visit jailed businessman.

text.p: U.S. consular officials in Shanghai on Monday visited U.S. businessman William Ping Chen, who was jailed last month for 10 years for illegally importing garbage into China, a U.S. consulate spokesman said.

Chen, born in Shanghai and now a resident of Oakland, California, was sentenced to deportation and a 500,000 yuan ($60,000) fine as well as the jail term after confessing to smuggling 238 tonnes of garbage and medical waste into Shanghai.
He has appealed against the sentence.

The consular official said he had no further information about Chen or when his appeal would be heard. An official from the Shanghai People's High Court also said he had no new information on the case.
Chen, 56, was arrested in June last year and was sentenced following a hearing on December 2. The official Xinhua news agency said he pleaded guilty to the charges.

Chen's arrest was the climax of an emotional campaign launched by China in mid-1996 over illegal shipments of U.S. garbage listed as waste paper for recycling but found to contain old clothes, rubber gloves, and disposable syringes.

Chen had listed the imports as waste paper and mixed paper, and proceeded with the shipments despite warnings from Shanghai environmental officials and opposition from his Chinese joint venture partners, Xinhua said.
